_meta.title: Effects starter database
_meta.purpose: Function-to-effect mapping for TRIZ synthesis: given a required function, find candidate physical, chemical, or geometric effects that deliver it.
_meta.provenance: Repository-authored summaries of established phenomena. External reference text is not reproduced. Entry references support targeted corrections and additions; unchanged legacy entries retain the original general textbook provenance.
_meta.usage: Search all installed packs with triz_effects. Categories organize retrieval; related_effects records useful general/special-case links. Typings are explicit hypotheses, not sufficiency verdicts.

audit.scope: Screened the original 60 entries for obvious conflation, misleading guarantees, classification errors and retrieval gaps; targeted source checks support corrections and additions.
remaining_gaps: Some effects remain untyped because a useful single-input/output contract has not been selected.
Opaque optical and field excitations deliberately lack SI dimensions until their quantitative interpretation is selected.
Most legacy entries still lack a specific per-entry external reference; conditional typings are not independent expert validation.

typing.source: Existing statements/functions and linked references, with SI declarations cross-checked against NIST SP 811.
typing.scope: One selected input/output clause per effect; conditions name other resources or operating assumptions. No behavior, feasibility, efficiency or sufficiency is inferred.

effects.name: Thermal expansion
effects.function: convert temperature change into displacement or force
effects.statement: Materials change dimension predictably with temperature; joined dissimilar metals bend when heated.
hints: shrink-fit assembly by heating or cooling
conditions: specified material and unconstrained expansion direction

effects.name: Photoelectric emission
effects.function: emit electrons from a surface with light and collect a photocurrent
effects.statement: Photons above a material-dependent emission threshold can eject electrons from a surface; a suitable collection circuit can measure a photocurrent.
effects.source: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-3/pages/6-2-photoelectric-effect ; surface emission with collected photocurrent ; explicit SI declarations: https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-chapter-4-two-classes-si-units-and-si-prefixes

effects.name: Photoluminescence and phosphorescence
effects.function: absorb light energy and release it later or shifted in color
effects.statement: Phosphors store absorbed energy and re-emit it as visible light, immediately or with delay.

effects.name: Total internal reflection
effects.function: guide light inside a medium and detect surface contact
effects.statement: Light stays trapped by reflection at a boundary until the boundary condition changes.

effects.name: Interference
effects.function: measure nanometer-scale differences by superposing waves
effects.statement: Overlapping coherent waves create fringes that encode tiny path differences.

effects.name: Diffraction
effects.function: spread waves by geometry and encode structure in the pattern
effects.statement: Waves bend around features comparable to their wavelength; the resulting pattern reveals the feature.

effects.name: Polarization
effects.function: filter light by orientation and reveal stress fields
effects.statement: Polarizers select components of light polarization; in suitable transparent materials, stress-induced birefringence changes relative optical phase and reveals stress patterns.
limitations: Stress analysis requires a suitable material and calibrated optical arrangement; polarization is not simply rotated by all transparent materials.

provenance.license: MIT (repository-authored summary; external reference text is not reproduced)

effects.name: Doppler effect
effects.function: detect relative velocity from a frequency shift
effects.statement: Relative motion between a wave source, reflector and receiver can shift the observed frequency; the shift depends on line-of-sight motion and wave propagation.
limitations: Simple proportional formulas have a limited velocity range; cosmological redshift is not a simple source-motion Doppler shift.

provenance.license: MIT (repository-authored summary; external reference text is not reproduced)

conditions: specified source frequency and propagation speed
velocity range appropriate to the declared Doppler model

effects.name: Bernoulli effect
effects.function: generate low pressure where flow speeds up
effects.statement: Along a streamline of steady, approximately incompressible, inviscid flow at equal elevation, an increase in speed corresponds to lower static pressure.
conditions: negligible viscous losses for the ideal relation
limitations: Pressure cannot be inferred from speed alone across arbitrary streamlines, elevations, pumps or lossy flow regions.

effects.name: Osmosis

effects.statement: Across a solvent-selective membrane, a concentration difference can drive solvent toward the more concentrated solution until an opposing pressure balances it.
hints: reverse-osmosis water purification with externally applied pressure
limitations: Reverse osmosis requires applied pressure exceeding the opposing osmotic pressure; ordinary osmosis does not purify water in that direction.

effects.name: Diffusion
effects.function: transport species along a concentration gradient
effects.statement: Atoms and molecules spread from high to low concentration, faster at higher temperature.

effects.name: Ultrasonic vibration
effects.function: transmit force through material via high-frequency waves
effects.statement: Above-audible vibrations clean, join, cut, and sense inside opaque material.

effects.name: Acoustic levitation
effects.function: hold matter in standing waves without contact
effects.statement: Sound pressure nodes can trap small particles or droplets in mid-air.

effects.name: Cavitation
effects.function: concentrate energy locally by bubble collapse
effects.statement: Vapor bubbles formed in low-pressure zones collapse violently where pressure recovers.

effects.name: Adsorption
effects.function: capture molecules on a high-area surface
effects.statement: High-area surfaces bind target molecules from a gas or liquid.

effects.name: Corona discharge and ionic wind
effects.function: move air or particles with an electric field
effects.statement: A sharp high-voltage point ionizes air; the ions drag air along and charge particles for collection.

effects.name: Eddy currents

effects.statement: Time-varying magnetic fields drive circulating currents that oppose motion and dissipate energy.

effects.name: Superconductivity
effects.function: carry direct current with zero electrical resistance within a superconducting operating range
effects.statement: Suitable materials have zero DC electrical resistance below material-dependent critical limits and exhibit superconducting magnetic behavior.
conditions: temperature, magnetic field and current within the material operating limits
limitations: Zero DC resistance does not mean a lossless complete system; cooling and time-varying operation can incur losses.

effects.name: Catalysis
effects.function: accelerate a reaction without being consumed
effects.statement: A catalyst lowers activation energy and emerges unchanged.

effects.name: Exothermic reaction
effects.function: release heat on demand
effects.statement: Certain reactions release large heat once triggered.

effects.name: Endothermic reaction
effects.function: absorb heat on demand
effects.statement: Dissolving or reacting certain species pulls heat from the surroundings.

effects.name: Polymerization
effects.function: solidify liquid monomers into a solid in place
effects.statement: Liquid precursors cure into a solid polymer on demand.

effects.name: Sacrificial oxidation
effects.function: protect a structure by consuming a cheaper reactive material
effects.statement: A more reactive metal corrodes preferentially, sparing the structure it is connected to.

effects.name: Colorimetric reaction
effects.function: make chemical state visible as a color change
effects.statement: Reagents change color in the presence of a target species at low concentration.

effects.name: Chemiluminescence

effects.statement: Some reactions emit light directly as they proceed.

effects.name: Hygroscopy
effects.function: absorb moisture from the environment
effects.statement: Certain materials take up water vapor, changing mass and mechanical properties as they do.

effects.name: Electroplating

effects.statement: Electric current reduces metal ions onto a conductive surface, building thickness layer by layer.

effects.name: Photopolymerization

effects.statement: Light cures a liquid resin locally and rapidly.

effects.name: Sublimation and deposition
effects.function: pass from solid directly to gas or deposit from gas to solid
effects.statement: At suitable temperature and pressure, a substance can pass directly between solid and vapor without an intervening liquid phase.
limitations: This is a physical phase change; decomposition or reaction into a gas is a different mechanism.

effects.name: Molecular sieve separation

effects.name: Combustion

effects.statement: An exothermic fuel-oxidizer reaction releases chemical energy; useful heat and pressure generation depend on the reaction products and operating arrangement.

effects.name: Wedge and inclined plane

effects.name: Lever

effects.name: Screw helix
effects.function: convert rotation into linear motion with mechanical advantage
effects.statement: A screw helix converts rotation into axial displacement and force; whether an axial load can back-drive it depends on lead angle and friction.
limitations: Self-locking is conditional, not an intrinsic property of every screw drive.

effects.name: Origami folding

effects.name: Vibration-assisted release
effects.function: release particles from a surface or remove a deposited layer by vibrating it
effects.statement: A vibrating surface can detach particles or deposits through inertial loading; release depends on adhesion, excitation and the mechanical response of the deposit.
hints: vibratory bin activators that free sticking bulk solids
rapping heat-exchanger tubes to shed fouling
limitations: Mass times peak acceleration is only a screening estimate, not a universal detachment criterion.

effects.name: Reverse-flow (back-pulse) cleaning
effects.function: remove a deposited layer from a porous surface or channel by reversing the flow through it
effects.statement: Drag and the pressure difference across a deposit point along the flow that built it up; a short pulse of reverse flow turns them around, lifting the deposited layer and carrying its particles away from the surface.
hints: backwashing granular media beds in water treatment
purging clogged sensing lines and nozzles

effects.name: Electrostatic repulsion
effects.function: release particles from a surface or keep them off it with like charges
effects.statement: Like charges repel; with a suitable charge distribution, electrostatic forces can lift particles when they exceed opposing adhesion and other forces.
hints: electrostatic dust detachment under controlled charging
limitations: Repulsion must overcome adhesion and other forces; traveling-field electrodynamic screens also use field gradients and are a separate mechanism.

effects.name: Thermal-expansion mismatch detachment

effects.statement: A layer and substrate with different expansion coefficients develop mismatch strain as temperature changes; the resulting stress can crack or detach the layer.

releasing ice or wax by brief heating
limitations: Mismatch strain does not guarantee release; bond strength, geometry and material response determine the result.

effects.function: transfer heat through a material or contact without bulk fluid transport
effects.statement: A temperature gradient drives conductive heat transfer; the rate depends on conductivity, geometry and interface resistance.

provenance.license: MIT (repository-authored summary; external reference text is not reproduced)

conditions: a thermal path and a temperature difference
specified conductive path and boundary temperatures
limitations: Contact resistance and temperature-dependent properties affect performance.

effects.name: Convection
effects.function: transport heat with a moving fluid
effects.statement: Bulk fluid motion transports thermal energy; motion may be forced externally or driven by buoyancy.

provenance.license: MIT (repository-authored summary; external reference text is not reproduced)

specified fluid motion, geometry and heat-transfer conditions
limitations: Heat transfer depends on flow regime, geometry and fluid properties; forced flow needs a driving resource.

effects.name: Thermal radiation

effects.name: Joule heating
effects.function: convert electrical energy into heat in a resistive conductor
effects.statement: Current through an electrical resistance dissipates power as heat; an ohmic resistor has instantaneous power I squared times R.

provenance.license: MIT (repository-authored summary; external reference text is not reproduced)

conditions: an electrical supply and a resistive path
limitations: Resistance changes with material and temperature; allowable current and heat rejection constrain operation.

effects.function: support or separate objects through the pressure gradient in a fluid
